newsitem.title: FRANCE: French authorities do not have BA move request.
newsitem.headline: French authorities do not have BA move request.

text.p: French authorities said on Wednesday they had not received a request from British Airways to move its Paris services from Charles de Gaulle airport due to security concerns and doubted whether such a request could be met.

Neither the transport ministry nor the Paris airport authority had received the demand, spokesmen from each said. The airports spokesman said British Airways was itself a security risk because of threats from the Irish Republican Army (IRA).

British Airways has said it wanted to shift its operations to Orly because security was insufficient after Air Algerie resumed flights to and from Paris last week and opened check-in desks alongside those of British Airways.

Charles Reder, spokesman for airport authority Aeroports de Paris (ADP), said it might not be possible to accommodate the large number of British Airways flights at Orly, which is smaller than Charles de Gaulle.
"It would be a bit difficult," Reder said. "At peak hours there are no more slots."

ADP would be responsible for planning to accommodate at Orly the 60-odd daily British Airways flights now operating from Charles de Gaulle, but the transport ministry would have to make to decision to allow the move.

Reder added that ADP and the government were making every effort to assure security at Charles de Gaulle and that in any case British Airways was itself a security risk and should not be pointing the finger at Air Algerie.

"There are threats against Air Algerie, but there are also threats against British Airways. They have their problems with the IRA," Reder said. "It's always possible to do more or do better, but it is difficult to transform an airport into a fortified camp," he said.

The transport ministry spokesman said he was aware of British Airways' plan only from news reports. He added it might be difficult to make such a move since there was little room to schedule more flights at Orly.
A French judge refused to rule on Tuesday on British Airways' bid to win tighter security at Charles de Gaulle, saying the airport was outside its geographical jurisdiction.
It transferred the case to an administrative court in Melun, south-east of Paris. Charles de Gaulle is north of Paris.
Air Algerie could not be reached for comment.

British Airways has been closing its counters at Charles de Gaulle for several hours a day since the weekend after Air Algerie resumed flights from Paris after a two-year break, opening check-in desks alongside those of British Airways.
Air Algerie suspended Paris flights two years ago in protest at being forced to use a remote terminal after Moslem radicals hijacked an Air France plane in Algiers at Christmas 1995.
